subject: English
passage: Scientists have long theorized that the collapse of Easter Island's civilization was caused by deforestation resulting from the inhabitants cutting down palm trees to transport massive stone statues. One archaeologist decided to investigate this theory. Working with a team of volunteers, she attempted to move replica statues across the island using only ropes—no wooden rollers or sledges. The replicas, weighing several tons each, were successfully transported upright using a coordinated rocking motion. This led the archaeologist to conclude that the statue transportation likely required far fewer trees than previously assumed.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To highlight the importance of recent discoveries in a field where experts have reached conflicting conclusions
choices.B: To evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of the approach taken in a scientific study
choices.C: To describe an experiment whose results cast doubt on an established hypothesis
choices.D: To compare two rival theories and describe the evidence supporting each position

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because it most accurately states the main purpose of the text, which is to describe an experiment whose results cast doubt on an established hypothesis. The text begins by noting that scientists have long believed that Easter Island's civilization collapsed due to deforestation from transporting stone statues with wooden tools. The text then describes an experiment conducted by an archaeologist to test this theory. According to the text, the results of the experiment led the archaeologist to conclude that statue transportation likely required far fewer trees than previously assumed. The archaeologist's results cast doubt on the long-held theory presented at the beginning of the text and suggest that deforestation may not have been the primary cause of the civilization's collapse.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect because the text addresses only one theory, that Easter Island's collapse was caused by deforestation from statue transportation. Rather than present a rival theory, the text explains how one archaeologist designed an experiment to test this long-held belief.
